1. Case 1: Left thalamic hemorrhage (IVH)
Acute right-sided facial and limb deficits with CT evidence of hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and intraventricular extension confirm hemorrhagic stroke. DTI showing a thinner left corticobulbar tract explains the right-sided deficits. MRI reveals no brainstem lesion, and CT refutes tumor/abscess and inflammatory/demyelinating processes, lowering those alternatives. The patient's hypertension history and typical hemorrhage location support hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage as a plausible mechanism, but direct blood pressure measurement and exclusion of other hemorrhagic causes are not documented, so the specific etiology remains less certain. The current frontier is sufficiently refined to answer the core diagnostic question.
